Slide 8A: Rendering Lifecycle: Trigger ➔ Render ➔ Commit
shortTitle: Trigger ➔ Render ➔ Commit Lifecycle
qText: What are the 3 Phases: Trigger ➔ Render ➔ Commit?
bullets: Step 1: Trigger: Initial mount or state update (setState) schedules a render task with the scheduler.
Step 2: Render (Reconciliation): React invokes component functions, constructs new Virtual DOM, and diffs with previous tree. Pure calculation with zero DOM mutations. Interruptible in React Fiber!
Step 3: Commit Phase: React applies calculated mutations (insert, update, delete) to the browser DOM. Synchronous and un-interruptible.
Browser Paint: Browser recalculates layout (Reflow) and paints pixels onto the screen.

name: Slide 8B: React Fiber Engine Architecture & Fiber Node
shortTitle: React Fiber Architecture & Linked List Tree
qText: What is React Fiber and Fiber Node structure?
bullets: Why Fiber? Old Stack reconciler was recursive and synchronous; large trees blocked the browser main thread and dropped frames.
Fiber Node: Fiber turns the call stack into a linked-list data structure that can be paused, prioritized, and resumed.
3 Key Pointers: Every Fiber node holds child (first child), sibling (next sibling), and return (parent).
Time-Slicing: Fiber breaks heavy rendering into 5ms chunks. High priority tasks (keystrokes) jump ahead of low priority tasks (lists).

name: Slide 8C: Fiber Double Buffering (Current vs WIP Tree)
shortTitle: Current Tree vs Work-in-Progress Tree
qText: How does Double Buffering prevent UI flickering?
bullets: Current Tree: The Fiber tree currently visible and mounted on the browser screen.
Work-in-Progress (WIP) Tree: Built asynchronously in background RAM during the Render Phase.
Instant Pointer Swap: On Commit, React swaps root.current = workInProgress in a single pointer operation (0ms latency).
No Half-Baked UI: If a render is aborted due to an error, the WIP tree is discarded and the user sees no broken screen!

name: Slide 8D: Reconciliation & Diffing Algorithm Rules
shortTitle: Reconciliation & Diffing Algorithm Rules ($O(n)$)
qText: What are the Heuristic Rules of the Diffing Algorithm?
bullets: $O(n)$ Linear Complexity: Traditional tree diffing takes $O(n^3)$. React uses 2 heuristic assumptions to achieve blazing fast $O(n)$ speed:
Rule 1 (Different Types): Two elements of different types produce different trees. Changing <div> to <section> destroys the entire old tree and rebuilds.
Rule 2 (Keys for Lists): Children with keys are matched across renders. React detects insertions, moves, and deletions without rebuilding the entire list.

name: Slide 8E: React 18 Auto Batching & StrictMode Double Render
shortTitle: Auto Batching & Strict Mode Double Render
qText: How does Automatic Batching & Strict Mode work?
bullets: Automatic Batching (React 18): Updates inside setTimeout, promises, and native event handlers are grouped into a single re-render (React 17 only batched React handlers).
Opting Out of Batching: Use flushSync(() => setState()) if immediate synchronous DOM read is needed.
StrictMode Double Render: In development, React intentionally mounts ➔ unmounts ➔ mounts to catch impure side-effects and missing cleanups.

bullets: Cross-Browser Wrapper: SyntheticEvent wraps native browser events so they work identically across Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge.

Return False Doesn't Work: You must call e.preventDefault() explicitly; return false does not prevent default in React.

Slide 24A: The children Prop: Content Projection & Wrappers
shortTitle: The children Prop & Wrapper Pattern
qText: What is the children Prop in React?
bullets: Content Projection: children is a special prop automatically passed to components that represents the JSX nested between opening and closing tags.
Generic Wrapper Components: Powers generic containers like <Card>, <Modal>, <Layout> without hardcoding specific child components.
Performance Benefit: Children passed from parent don't re-render when the wrapper component's internal state updates!

name: Slide 24B: Component Composition vs Prop Drilling (Slot Pattern)
shortTitle: Component Composition Patterns
qText: How does Component Composition solve Prop Drilling without Context?
bullets: Composition over Inheritance: React docs famously state: 'At Facebook, we use React in thousands of components, and we haven't found any use cases where we would recommend creating component inheritance hierarchies.'
Slot Pattern: You can pass components themselves as props (e.g. topBar={<Header/>}, sidebar={<Menu/>}).
Eliminates Intermediate Props: Intermediate components don't even need to know what props the leaf component requires!

name: Slide 27B: One-Way Data Flow (Unidirectional Flow) in React
shortTitle: One-Way Data Flow (Unidirectional Flow)
qText: What is One-Way Data Flow (Unidirectional Flow)?
bullets: Top-Down Strict Direction: Data flows strictly from parent to child via props. A child component can NEVER mutate its parent's state directly.
Why is it Beneficial? Predictable debugging! If a bug occurs in state, you only need to inspect the owner component, not 20 different children.
Inverse Data Flow: To pass data back up, parent passes a callback function down via props (e.g. onPatientSelect={handleSelect}).
Versus Angular/Vue: Traditional frameworks used 2-way data binding (changes in child auto-mutated parent model), making large app state unpredictable.

name: Slide 27C: State Lifting: Synchronizing Sibling Components
shortTitle: State Lifting Architecture
qText: How does State Lifting synchronize Sibling Components?
bullets: The Problem: Two sibling components (e.g. SearchBar and PatientTable) need to share search query state, but siblings cannot talk to each other directly.
The Solution: Lift the state up to their closest common parent component.
Data Down, Events Up: Parent passes the query down to PatientTable via props, and passes setQuery down to SearchBar via callback prop.

name: Slide 27D: Immutable State Updates: Objects & Arrays Patterns
shortTitle: Immutable State Updates: Objects & Arrays
qText: How to perform Immutable State Updates for Complex Objects & Arrays?
bullets: Never Use Mutating Methods: Avoid push, pop, splice, reverse, sort directly on state array.
Use Safe Pure Methods: Use map, filter, concat, and spread [...arr].
Nested Objects: Shallow spread only copies top-level properties; nested objects must be spread explicitly.
Library Helper: For deep trees, use Immer (produce) to write natural code safely.

name: Slide 27E: Why Direct State Mutation is Wrong in React
shortTitle: Why Direct State Mutation is Wrong
qText: Why is Direct State Mutation Wrong in React?
bullets: Referential Comparison: React checks Object.is(oldState, newState). Direct mutation keeps the exact same memory pointer, so React assumes nothing changed and skips re-rendering!
Time-Travel & DevTools Broken: Direct mutation overwrites the past state history in memory, breaking undo/redo and debugging.
Async Race Conditions: React batches updates. Mutating state causes concurrent readers to see half-mutated data.
Golden Rule: Always return a newly created object or array using spread {...old}, [...old], or Immer.

Slide 45A: Lists and Keys: Reconciliation & Why Index is an Anti-Pattern
shortTitle: Lists and Keys: Reconciliation & Index Trap
qText: Why is using Array Index as Key an Anti-Pattern?
bullets: Reconciliation Identity: React uses key to identify which item in a list changed, was added, or was deleted.
Index Key Hazard: If you insert an item at the top of an array, every existing item's index shifts (index 0 becomes 1).
UI State Corruption: Input field focus, checkbox checked state, and animations get associated with the wrong item!
When is Index Acceptable? ONLY if list is 100% static (never sorted, never filtered, never deleted).

Slide 76A: useRef Hook: DOM Access & Persistent Values
shortTitle: useRef Hook: DOM Access & Persistence
qText: What is the useRef Hook and its 2 Core Use Cases?
bullets: Use Case 1: Direct DOM Access: Focusing input fields, measuring scroll heights, managing canvas, triggering media play/pause.
Use Case 2: Mutable Value without Re-render: Storing timer IDs, previous state values, render counts. Mutating ref.current = newVal does NOT trigger a re-render!
Memory Pointer: The returned object { current: value } persists across the entire lifecycle of the component instance.

name: Slide 76B: useReducer Hook: Complex State Management
shortTitle: useReducer: Complex State Management
qText: When should you use useReducer instead of useState?
bullets: Complex State Logic: When state involves multiple sub-values, nested objects, or when next state depends on previous state.
Decoupled Actions: Separates 'what happened' (dispatch action) from 'how state updates' (reducer function).
Passing Dispatch Down: Dispatch function has a stable identity and never changes across re-renders, optimizing child component performance.
Mini-Redux locally: Provides Redux-like predictable state management within a single component tree without adding external packages.

name: Slide 76C: useEffect vs useLayoutEffect (Paint Timing)
shortTitle: useEffect vs useLayoutEffect Comparison
qText: What is the difference between useEffect and useLayoutEffect?
tableRows: Can cause visible flicker if measuring DOM dimensions
Zero flicker; pauses paint until DOM measurements finish
Non-blocking; does not freeze UI thread
Blocking; slows down paint if calculation is slow

name: Slide 76D: useTransition & useDeferredValue in React 18
shortTitle: useTransition vs useDeferredValue (Concurrent)
qText: How do useTransition & useDeferredValue optimize UI responsiveness?
bullets: Urgent vs Transition: Urgent updates (typing input, clicking tabs) need instant response. Transition updates (filtering 5,000 items) can lag without blocking the UI.
useTransition: Wraps a state setter: startTransition(() => setQuery(text)). Gives isPending spinner indicator.
useDeferredValue: Wraps a value directly: const deferredQuery = useDeferredValue(query). Defers re-rendering dependent components.
Result: Search typing never stutters, even while filtering massive datasets!

name: Slide 76E: Rules of Hooks, Stale Closures & Infinite Loops
shortTitle: Rules of Hooks & Stale Closures Trap
qText: What are Stale Closures and how to avoid them?
bullets: Stale Closure Trap: Occurs when useEffect, useCallback, or setTimeout captures an old state snapshot.
Why it Happens: JavaScript functions close over variables in their lexical scope at creation time.
The Fix 1: Always use functional state updater setCount(prev => prev + 1).
The Fix 2: Include all referenced reactive values inside the dependency array.

bullets: The Flaw: In Context API, all components calling useContext(MyContext) re-render whenever ANY value in the context object changes.
The Scenario: A component that only dispatches an action still re-renders whenever state changes if both are in the same context!
The Architecture Fix: Split into two contexts: StateContext (for data consumers) and DispatchContext (for action triggers).

name: Slide 81B: Race Conditions & AbortController in API Calls
shortTitle: Race Conditions & AbortController Fix
qText: How to prevent Race Conditions with AbortController?
bullets: The Problem: User clicks Tab A then Tab B quickly. Tab A's slower response arrives after Tab B, displaying wrong stale data!
AbortController Solution: Create an AbortController instance in useEffect.
Cleanup Hook: Call controller.abort() in cleanup. Cancels pending network request instantly when deps change or component unmounts.

name: Slide 81C: Debouncing vs Throttling in API Integration
shortTitle: Debouncing vs Throttling Comparison
qText: What is the difference between Debouncing and Throttling?
tableRows: Delays execution until user **stops typing** for N ms
Executes function at most once every N ms interval
Fires at fixed periodic rate during continuous activity
Window scrolling, game loop, mouse move
Saves 95% of unnecessary network API calls
Ensures smooth UI updates without freezing thread

qText: What are Error Boundaries & How do they prevent White Screen of Death?
bullets: The Problem: In React 16+, an uncaught JavaScript error in any component unmounts the entire component tree, causing a completely blank white screen.
Error Boundary: A class component that catches JavaScript errors anywhere in its child component tree and displays a fallback UI.
Lifecycle Methods: Uses static getDerivedStateFromError() to render fallback UI and componentDidCatch() to log error telemetry (Sentry).

qText: Why and when should you use ReactDOM.createPortal?

Portal Solution: ReactDOM.createPortal(children, domNode) inserts the modal directly into document.body outside the parent DOM hierarchy.
React Event Bubbling Preserved: Even though the DOM node lives in document.body, React events bubble up the React component tree naturally!

Slide 124A: Referential Equality & Stable References (Object.is)
shortTitle: Referential Equality & Stable Object References
qText: Why does Referential Equality break React.memo?
bullets: Memory Reference Check: JavaScript compares objects and functions by memory address, not value ({} !== {}).
Re-creation on Render: Every time a parent renders, inline objects style={{color:'red'}} and inline functions () => doWork() are given new memory addresses.
React.memo Breakdown: React.memo does shallow equality (oldProp === newProp). Since pointers differ, it re-renders the child anyway!
The Fix: Use useCallback for callbacks and useMemo for objects passed to memoized children.

Slide 129A: Redux Fundamentals & Architecture Flow
shortTitle: Redux Architecture & Complete Unidirectional Data Flow
qText: What is Redux and the Complete Data Flow?
bullets: Single Source of Truth: Entire global state of the app is stored in an object tree inside a single Store.
State is Read-Only: The only way to change state is to emit an Action (an object describing what happened).
Pure Reducer Functions: Reducers take (previousState, action) => newState and must be 100% pure with 0 side-effects.
Unidirectional Flow: UI Event ➔ dispatch(action) ➔ Reducer calculates new state ➔ Store updates ➔ Subscribed UI re-renders!

name: Slide 129C: Redux Toolkit (RTK) configureStore & createSlice
shortTitle: configureStore & createSlice Architecture
qText: How does createSlice eliminate boilerplate?
bullets: No Action Creators Needed: createSlice automatically generates action creators and action type strings from reducer names.
Immer Built-in: You write code that looks like direct mutation (state.count += 1), but Immer safely produces a new immutable copy!
configureStore: Automatically sets up Redux DevTools, Redux Thunk, and combines reducers with zero manual config.

name: Slide 129D: createAsyncThunk & extraReducers Lifecycle
shortTitle: createAsyncThunk & extraReducers Lifecycle
qText: How does createAsyncThunk handle API lifecycles?
bullets: Why Not in Reducers? Reducers must remain 100% synchronous and pure. Async operations belong in Thunk middleware.
Automatic 3 States: Generates pending, fulfilled, and rejected action types automatically.
extraReducers: Slice listens to thunk actions using the builder callback syntax.

name: Slide 129E: RTK Query: Automated Caching & Tags Invalidation
shortTitle: RTK Query: Auto Caching & Tags Invalidation
qText: How does RTK Query manage server cache & invalidation?
bullets: Server State vs Client State: APIs are server cache, not client UI state. RTK Query manages data fetching, caching, and deduplication automatically.
Auto-generated Hooks: useGetPatientsQuery() gives data, isLoading, isError, refetch instantly.
Tags Cache Invalidation: Query provides tags (providesTags: ['Patients']). Mutation invalidates tags (invalidatesTags: ['Patients']), which automatically refetches data!
